writeup: TIC 65085092 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.424 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 6.84% dimming, while a secondary eclipse was not detected. The detection carries a high signal-to-noise ratio of 307.4 in the Box Least Squares periodogram, and pixel-level image analysis confirms the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 29.5, though the centroid offset of 3.0 arcseconds warrants note. The target does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a significant data quality flag indicates that alternating eclipses differ substantially in depth, suggesting the true period may be twice the initial detection - a pattern consistent with eclipses of unequal depth rather than a simple binary orbit.
